name: default
description: Default specification baseline of high-quality agent outputs
examples: Here is a clear and concise analysis of the project requirements, identifying the core MVP components, functional stories, and non-functional bounds. We have established that tracking embedding distance against a fixed baseline centroid is our primary metric.

The statistical validation plan compares fresh-context baseline output against a saturated, off-topic pollutant context to calibrate the cosine distance threshold. Page-Hinkley and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests will be evaluated in future iterations.

Our design prioritises low runtime overhead, using lightweight sentence embeddings to calculate cosine similarity. If the similarity drops below our pre-calibrated threshold, an inline notice is emitted immediately in the CLI session.
The integration wraps the base LLM client, intercepting incoming and outgoing request objects to transparently measure turn latency.
We configure the online feature extractor to calculate the vocabulary repetition rate using a rolling window of recent words.
Our system measures format compliance by matching the JSON output keys against the predefined Pydantic schema.
The ADWIN detector dynamically scales its monitoring window, triggering alarms only when statistical distribution shifts occur.
To preserve model intelligence, the agent recommends summary compaction when context tokens exceed the smart zone limit.
We enforce structured output formatting across all turns by validating required system keywords in the model's response.
The calibration harness runs prompt evaluations on clean configurations to establish a baseline semantic variance.
We monitor the cumulative token count per turn to map output drift against the filling context window size.
A sustained-trend detector processes the sequence of similarity metrics to distinguish noise from true degradation.
The metrics logger serializes cosine distance, execution overhead, and timestamp metadata into a local JSON Lines file.
Local embedding models are integrated via a pluggable adapter, reducing network dependencies and API call overhead.
We evaluate the accuracy gap by comparing correct answers on fresh probes with results from context-polluted prompts.
The warning system logs a non-blocking diagnostic notification when similarity metrics drop near the calibration boundary.
We isolate variables by testing pure saturation effects with random characters against semantic drift from off-topic inputs.
L2 normalization is applied to all embedding vectors to ensure distance calculations represent directional meaning changes.
We configure the offline test harness to generate ROC curves and calibrate optimal decision bounds on validation datasets.
The middleware decorator intercepts prompt sequences and injects inline alerts directly into the developer console.
